blocks.h2: Why Sewer Lines Fail in Hanover Park
blocks.intro: Hanover Park grew from 451 residents in 1960 to more than 28,000 by 1980. Most of its sewer lines date from that boom.

items.body: Some homes from this era used pipe that can sag, crack or deform with age.
Pipe laid in backfill can sink and form low spots that hold waste.
Trees planted in the '70s are now big enough to reach the line.
Gaps where roots and soil get in.
Lines under driveways are a good fit for trenchless repair.

blocks.intro: We show you the problem before we fix it.

blocks.h2: How We Repair a Sewer Line
blocks.intro: Once we know what's wrong, there's usually more than one way to fix it. Which method makes sense depends on the pipe's condition, location, and how it failed.
head: Method
What It Involves
Typical Disruption
rows: A resin-coated liner is pulled through the existing pipe and cured in place, creating a new pipe inside the old one.
Minimal digging, usually just small access points
A new pipe is pulled through the old one while a bursting head fractures the old pipe outward to make room.
Minimal digging, works even when the old pipe is badly damaged
The damaged section is dug up and replaced directly.
More digging, but sometimes the only option depending on damage location and access
blocks.note: Most Hanover Park lots have lawns and driveways over the line. The footage tells us whether we can avoid digging them up.

blocks.h2: What a Sewer Repair Looks Like in Hanover Park
blocks.body: Most repairs start with a locate. The camera head carries a transmitter, so we can mark the exact spot on your lawn and know how deep the problem sits before anyone picks up a shovel. A single cracked joint is often a one-day spot repair with a small hole. A long run of root-damaged pipe is usually lined instead. If a section has sunk, we dig and reset it at the right slope, then restore the soil. Either way, you'll know the plan, the footprint and the price before work starts.

blocks.h2: Sewer Repair Questions From Hanover Park Homeowners

items.q: My house is from the '70s. Is the sewer line wearing out?
items.preview: It may be. A camera shows for sure.
items.answer: It may be. Many lines from that era are still fine, while others have sagged or cracked. A [camera inspection](/hanover-park/video-camera-sewer-inspections) settles it.

items.q: What's a belly in a sewer line?
items.preview: A low spot where pipe has settled.
items.answer: A section that has sunk, so waste and water sit there instead of draining. Small ones can be watched. Big ones need repair.

items.q: Can you fix it without digging up the yard?
items.answer: Often. [Trenchless repair](/hanover-park/trenchless-sewer-repair) works through small openings, though a bad belly may need digging.

items.q: Who is responsible for the sewer line?
items.preview: The homeowner, from the house to the main.
items.answer: In most cases, the homeowner owns the line from the house to the public sewer.

items.q: How long does a sewer repair take?
items.preview: Often one day for a spot repair.
items.answer: A spot repair is often done in a day. Lining or replacing a longer section can take a day or two, depending on access and permits.

items.q: Will you fix my lawn after digging?
items.answer: We backfill and level the area. Grass and landscaping take a season to fill back in, so we plan the opening to keep it small.

items.q: How much does sewer repair cost in Hanover Park?
items.preview: It depends on the damage and method. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on what the camera shows, the depth and the method. You'll approve a flat-rate price before any work.
